Classify errors and debug game rules

Unit 1 · Week 9 · Lesson 2 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the current Year 11 project brief, project-workbook.md, project-milestones.csv, project-test-log.csv and the selected scenario starter in project-pack.zip. Check the four S01 preparation exits first. Use the shared FR/NFR contract at https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/assessments/games/year11-requirements.md . Keep school-issued support, assessment and submission conditions visible. Use a disposable local folder, synthetic labels, primitive shapes and permitted static assets. Suggested times are untrialled; record actual completion/support and re-plan openly if needed.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

Current project workbook · Shared game requirements · Project test log · Ten workshop milestones

1. Find a fault and verify the repair

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Theory/debugging practice before the next two build workshops. Use small disposable examples; do not alter important data or supply a complete assessed-game repair. 2. Retrieve a testable requirement

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval and explanation

A successful run can violate a requirement. Derive expected states from the common contract and independent reasoning. Rerunning earlier cases after a repair checks for regressions. 3. Classify the failure before guessing

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Classification sort and teacher modelling

SyntaxError is itself a Python exception class; here distinguish parsing from exceptions during ordinary execution. A wrong score may produce no exception. Use a missing colon, a bad list index and an accumulator replacement as separate practice examples. Current chapter: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design . 4. Use the traceback to narrow the cause

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Predict, run and inspect

There are five entries with indices0..4; active[5] raises IndexError. Read the actual editor traceback, whose wording can vary by version. Do not mask the fault with a blanket handler. Decide the operation’s contract before choosing a corrected index; an empty list needs separate handling. Current chapter: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design . 5. Trace the first wrong score

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher think-aloud and paired trace

The faulty snippet prints10 after each pass, while the independent expected totals are10 then20. total=10 replaces rather than accumulates. This is an isolated accumulator fault; it does not implement the game’s once-only guard or full scoring contract. Learners explain the cause before proposing a correction and rerun empty/one/two-collection cases. Current chapter: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design . 6. Repair one cause and keep the evidence

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent debugging clinic

Use disposable code for the guided clinic. In the project, each student makes their own permitted change and records support. Retest repeated collection, first/last item, empty history, pause/reset and previously passing cases as relevant. Do not infer the whole game is correct from one repaired output. 7. What counts as a useful repair?

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Hinge question and counterexample

B. Suppressing a symptom can leave data/state wrong and hide errors. Ask learners for an observable expected result and a regression case, not just the option letter. 8. Explain a fresh fault

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent exit and next step

Use a teacher-selected fresh practice example; record reasoning and next action. Next lesson resumes score/lives/timing implementation under the existing project conditions.
